title: Title page: checked, subtitles ready
note: The tags say what the default copy really is (SPEC 5): filled with a tick = checked. The Version pill names the real best copy ("best of 4"). v1.1: the pill names the one subtitle that will show (English); the source and "Icelandic ready too" sit at the end of the pill row, so the page keeps the app's height and More like this stays at 366 (M4).

title: Title page: first visit, checking
note: Until a copy is checked its tag is what the name says: dashed, no tick. One copy at a time, never more streams than the provider allows (SPEC 5.3). v1.1: Play never waits for a check (S11): it plays the best copy known now; a later result is for the next Play. The only wait before Play is the add-ons' one (SPEC 5.5).

title: The Copies menu
note: OK on the Version pill. "Always the best copy" is the default and focused. Each copy shows what the check found: the "4K UHD" one is 1080p at 2.8 Mb/s; the Dolby Vision one is last, as its only sound can't play here. v1.1: Mb/s is the picture's share (S5); a different cut would read "Longer cut · 3 h 20 min" and never be picked by "Always the best" (S6).

title: The Subtitles sheet
note: OK on the Subtitles pill. v1.1 (M1): no ticks here. This copy's fingerprint isn't known to OpenSubtitles, so English was only lined up with other subtitles, and the Icelandic speed fix follows the copy's frame rate but its offset doesn't. A tick appears only for "Made for this copy" or "Lined up with this copy". The heading has 8 px of air above the ring (M7).

title: Subtitles: which film is it?
note: v1.1 (M3, S7, S9): only asked when nothing else can decide. "EN| The Lion King" has no year; two IMDb films have that name; and this copy couldn't be checked (its provider refuses partial reads), so its length can't pick one. With a checked length, a single candidate within 5% is accepted without asking. A dubbed copy is never asked about: its subtitles default to off.

title: Which film is this?
note: Rows: title / year · length · director (real Cinemeta meta, one /meta call per row; S9). With a checked length the closest row is focused; with none, as here, the first result is, and the header says the length is unknown. "None of these" turns OpenSubtitles off for this title. The add-ons design uses this same menu.

title: Subtitles: OpenSubtitles isn't answering
note: The add-on is down (or slow: 8 s). The pill row says so and when it tries again; nothing to press. Play still works: subtitles that come in later appear in the player, which says so once (SPEC 7.6). Lists already fetched are kept for 2 days.

title: A series: subtitles per episode
note: v1.1: the app's real layout (plot, chips at 272, rail at 318), with nothing added to its height (M4). The pill by Play describes the episode Play plays (S1 · E1); the focused tile's own subtitles go on its synopsis line (E2: English, from OpenSubtitles). Real: S1 E1 has 2 English files and no Icelandic.

title: Movies: checked and named tags
note: A filled tag is what airglow found in the best copy; a dashed one is only the provider's name. v1.1: no green ticks at poster size (S20), "1080p" as everywhere else. Dune: Part Two's copies are named 4K but checked as 1080p, so it leaves the 4K chip. Checks fill in slowly (title pages, Continue watching, Saved: SPEC 5.3), so most posters stay dashed: that's by design (M5).

title: Account: Languages
note: The one place for the defaults. v1.1 (S14): "Subtitles with sounds", not "Sound descriptions" (which reads like narration for blind viewers). Today's "Auto" becomes "Only when the sound isn't in your language" until the owner picks (S24). A dubbed copy in one of your languages gets no subtitles in another language (S7).

title: Play: the best copy starts
note: The controls show for 4 s when a film starts (as today). The title block gets one line: what the check found in the copy that is playing, that it was the best of 4, and the subtitles that are on. A copy picked by hand says "your pick" instead.

title: Options > Subtitles
note: CC, or ▼ then Subtitles. v1.1: "Early or late" sits right under the subtitle that's on, 1 press from it (S16); picking a row closes the panel with "Icelandic subtitles on · ▼, then Subtitles for timing". No ticks: nothing here was checked against this copy (M1). Plain words: "Timing fixed to fit this film" (S15), "with sounds" (S14).

title: Options > Subtitles: in the file and downloaded
note: The 1080p copy has English and Spanish in its file: they come first, ticked "Made for this copy" (airglow read them from the file). No "Early or late" row: it only appears under a downloaded subtitle that's on. The best English download stays listed (S2: an untagged file track can be another language).

title: Subtitles early or late
note: One small strip at the top (y 27 to 155), so the picture and the subtitle line stay in view. Each ◀ ▶ moves the subtitles 0.5 s (hold: 4 steps a second, up to 60 s), shown at once: airglow draws downloaded subtitles in its own view (SPEC 7.5). v1.1: ▲ reads "Undo my changes" (the automatic fix stays).

title: Match a line
note: When you can't tell if they're early or late: the strip shows the next line. OK when you hear it; the difference (less 0.3 s for the press) becomes the timing, rounded to 0.5 s, then the early/late strip comes back for a final step.

title: Downloaded subtitles, timing not checked
note: Shown once per film, 6 s, at the first downloaded line, only when nothing could line the file up (no fingerprint match, no two other files that agree: SPEC 3.4). Top right: this chip only; Up next keeps the kit's place (nit). No action, so OK stays Pause.

title: Options > Subtitles: OpenSubtitles down
note: The add-on is down and this copy has none. The panel says so, offers Try now, and points at the copy that has subtitles in its file (known from the check), which opens Quality. When subtitles come in later, one line says so: "English subtitles are ready · CC".

title: Options > Quality: the real copies
note: Today's panel (openQuality) with each copy's checked quality instead of its name, and the same "Always the best copy" default as the title page. Opening it never opens a stream: the rows are the cached checks. v1.1: 384 wide like Subtitles; the foot has room (S19).
